name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Lost in Permissions: Exploring the Microsoft 365 App Ecosystem
items.dek: Analysis of 8,000 Microsoft 365 third-party apps finds permission-functionality misalignment in 40% of cases via anomaly detection.
items.unproven: anomaly detection framework tuning on limited labeled examples; false positive rates when applied to new application cohorts; automated detection accuracy compared to manual security review

items.title: Measuring Post-Quantum TLS Deployment Across UK Internet Sectors
items.dek: Measurement of 4,665 UK organizations shows 44% HTTPS but only 6.4% SMTP post-quantum support; HTTPS 16.89x more common.
items.unproven: measurement captures only observable public endpoints; does not assess internal TLS migration or organizational readiness timelines; sector-specific barriers to SMTP deployment not identified

items.title: CVE-2026-18577 — N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
items.dek: N-able N-central. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 6 August.

items.title: Inverting the Hidden: Unveiling Multimodal Privacy Leakage in Collaborative LVLM Inference
items.dek: RASR attack recovers visual content from intermediate hidden states in collaborative LVLM inference by 50% better than prior methods, demonstrating privacy leak in edge-cloud deployments.
items.unproven: tested on two LVLM families; whether attack scales to production-grade defenses or white-box detection mechanisms

items.title: Registry Descriptions Go Stale Unevenly: An 89-Day Measurement of Model Context Protocol Drift, and Why Drift-Ranked Re-Auditing Under-Covers It
items.dek: MCP registry descriptions decay unevenly over 89 days; re-auditing high-drift servers catches only 20% of description changes versus 27% for random re-auditing.
items.unproven: limited to single registry; whether findings apply to other package ecosystems with different churn rates or governance models

items.title: A False Average: Chain-of-Thought Monitors Collapse Where They Are the Only Defense
items.dek: Rewriting chain-of-thought reasoning while preserving actions drops monitor catch rate from 95% to 11% on hacks where reasoning is the only defense signal.
items.unproven: attack is demonstrated on fixed Gemini proposals and lab agents; does not establish whether production monitors with external trace signals or live human oversight recover the defense substantially

items.title: Mutate to Bypass: Autonomous Endpoint Evasion via Knowledge-Driven Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.dek: AutoBypass multi-agent framework bypassed seven commercial EDR platforms with polymorphic payloads, reaching 90% evasion against Windows Defender.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to observed lab detections and alerts; patching velocity after disclosure unknown; red-team controls on payload staging and C2 communication unclear.

items.title: Why Formal Monitors Fail: Attack Distribution Entropy as a Coverage Bound for LTL-Based LLM Agent Safety
items.dek: Shannon entropy of attack distribution bounds FSA monitor recall; GPT models yield 0.24-bit concentrated patterns (96% in one), Gemini 2.81-bit dispersed (6–13% coverage).
items.unproven: Eight models tested but sample limited to frontier LLM classes; applicability to fine-tuned, specialized, or older model families unexamined.

items.title: SoK: Intent-Oriented Systematization of Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
items.dek: Multi-turn LLM jailbreaks organized by intent structure reveal that effectiveness depends on how intent unfolds across turns, not volume.
items.unproven: Limited to text-based LLMs; interaction patterns with agents in SDLC contexts and guardrail effectiveness under this taxonomy not measured.

items.title: Safety Invariants for Agents Orchestrating Irreversible State Transitions: A Four-Dimensional Formalism Evaluated on Public Ledgers
items.dek: Four-dimensional formalism with seven safety invariants guarantees irreversible ledger transitions execute exactly once, even under retry and delegation faults.
items.unproven: Whether execution-fidelity theorem holds when user-intent preview itself contains ambiguity; applicability to non-ledger irreversible state changes.

items.title: When Prompts Control Robots: Prompt Injection Attacks in Multi-Agent Robotic Systems
items.dek: Prompt injection in multi-agent robotic systems propagates across agents via shared prompts; first systematic study of cross-agent contamination.
items.unproven: Whether defenses tested on lab robotic rigs generalize to production hardware; long-horizon attack composition beyond single injection.

items.title: Adversarial Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines: Unveiling Structural Vulnerabilities in Agentic AI Architectures
items.dek: Multi-agent LLM pipelines lack inter-agent boundary verification, enabling content injection, impersonation, plan deviation, and memory poisoning from benign deployments.
items.unproven: Whether proposed boundary verification primitives can be retrofitted to existing production pipelines without latency penalty; defense effectiveness against composite attacks.

items.title: Domain Decoupling Attack: Exploiting the Validation Gap Between Protective DNS and Shared Edge Routing
items.dek: DNS-based validation gap allows reuse of shared IP authorization to reach co-tenant domains; 95.8% exposure rate across measured domains.
items.unproven: measurement scope is passive DNS and routing enumeration; does not demonstrate active exploitation or quantify real-world attack surface for any specific infrastructure operator

items.title: Antares: Foundation Models for Agentic Vulnerability Localization
items.dek: Antares compact models (350M–3B) for agentic vulnerability localization match GPT-4.5 while enabling local inference at $0.002 per task.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to repository-level vulnerability tasks; generalization to custom internal codebases and proprietary frameworks; false positive rates on real SAST pipelines

items.title: Benign Alone, Harmful Together: Exploiting Experience Composition in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.dek: EvoBreak attack decomposes multi-step safety violations into benign individual tasks that accumulate when agent self-evolves; requires synthesis of target dependency structures.
items.unproven: Laboratory attack on research agent frameworks; applicability to production LLM systems with robust memory isolation and audit trails unproven; BreakGym synthesis only covers synthetic targets.

items.title: Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance
items.dek: Framework mapping threat surface across single and multi-agent LLM deployments: prompt injection, memory, tool interfaces, delegation, model routing.
items.unproven: No concrete detection or mitigation techniques; scope is taxonomy and threat modeling rather than validated controls or measurement.

items.title: How Benchmarks and Evaluation Protocols Shape Conclusions in Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection
items.dek: Re-evaluation of provenance-based intrusion detection on DARPA TC E3 shows simple allowlist matches learned baselines; lexical novelty dominates measured performance.
items.unproven: Findings limited to audited DARPA datasets; applicability to production enterprise SOC telemetry and alert workflows unclear.

items.title: A Unified Benchmark for Privacy-preserving Vector Search
items.dek: Unified benchmark of four cryptographic vector-search schemes shows Pareto tradeoffs in privacy, performance, and recall rather than uniform penalties.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to single hardware class and synthetic workloads; production deployment patterns and actual corpus scale not tested.

items.title: An AI Approach to Verified Production Cryptographic Libraries
items.dek: AI system synthesizes proofs and internal specs for production cryptographic code, verifying curve25519-dalek and RustCrypto's chacha20 in 11.4 hours.
items.unproven: Single model family, two libraries; human verification of synthesized proofs not independent; scalability to larger codebases and other crypto primitives unknown.

items.title: NoisePQC++: A Unified NIST-Compliant PQC and Hybrid-PQC Implementation of the Noise Protocol
items.dek: CryptoProver verifies curve25519-dalek and ChaCha20 implementations using LLM-synthesized proofs in Verus, covering 57 classical and 13 post-quantum Noise handshake patterns.
items.unproven: proofs synthesized with fixed library of axioms trusted without independent audit; whether approach scales to cryptographic libraries without available specifications

items.title: Hardware-rooted attestation for AI-agent evidence: composing IETF RATS with action evidence packages
items.dek: Composite attestation binds hardware RATS appraisal to software action evidence packages to verify deployed model version produced agent output.
items.unproven: Practical deployment model when agent output timing does not align with measured-boot attestation cycles; whether Veraison performance scales to multi-agent scenarios.

items.title: Solving the Shortest Vector Problem in time $2^{0.6039n}$ Time via Mid-point Hessian
items.dek: Shortest vector problem solved in 2^0.6039n time, improving classical algorithms by exponential factor.
items.unproven: practical implementation on cryptographically relevant lattice dimensions; requires validation against deployed SVP solvers in real migration planning contexts

items.title: Agentic Incident Response through Digital Twin-Enhanced Multiscale Planning
items.dek: LLM agents for incident response planning combined with rollout planning to reduce hallucination and extend horizon.
items.unproven: evaluation against real incident datasets from financial services; integration with existing SOAR platforms; reliability guarantees in production deployment

items.title: Self-Supervised Representations for Binary Program Clustering: From Empirical Study to Retrieval-Augmented Learning
items.dek: VIME self-supervised learning achieves state-of-art binary malware clustering on Ember and Bodmas datasets.
items.unproven: evaluation on only two public datasets; applicability to proprietary malware families and organizational threat landscape; computational cost relative to supervised baselines

items.title: TurboRetry: Mitigating Large-Scale QUIC Handshake Floods with Off-the-Shelf DPU Offloading
items.dek: TurboRetry offloads QUIC Retry mechanism to DPUs to mitigate handshake floods without host CPU bottleneck.
items.unproven: evaluation limited to testbed; real-world deployment on production QUIC services; DPU availability across mainstream infrastructure providers; backward compatibility with existing clients

noise.title: Critical CVE issued for hallucinated SQLite vulnerability
noise.dek: CVE vulnerability analysis of SQLite hallucination illustrates supply-chain risk communication patterns.
noise.unproven: link text only; actual vulnerability details and exploitation scope not accessible in submission

noise.title: Devtools must be open source
noise.dek: Opinion piece arguing for open-source development tools; no evidence or novel argument.

noise.title: Utah produced more power from solar than any other source in May, a new first
noise.dek: Utah energy generation milestone; entirely outside application security and SDLC scope.
